expected_no_table_zones.location: 'Figure 4.' -- the Internet Datagram Header bit-field diagram
expected_no_table_zones.looks_like: a wide multi-column data table with a header row of column numbers
expected_no_table_zones.reason: The famous IP header bit-layout diagram: a row of bit-position numbers (0 through 31, wrapped across 4 lines of 0-9 digit sequences) followed by rows of +-+-+-+ separator lines and |Version|IHL|Type of Service|...| field-name cells. This is EXTREMELY table-like in raw text form (regular column separators, header-like numeric top row, cell-like bracketed field names) but is semantically a bit-field diagram, not tabular data in the normal sense -- a very strong test of the column-alignment false-positive risk named in the task brief.

expected_no_table_zones.location: Type of Service bit-field diagram (below section 3.1's field-by-field description)
expected_no_table_zones.looks_like: a small data table with a header row (0-7) and one data row of single-letter codes
expected_no_table_zones.reason: A second, smaller bit-field diagram: a row of bit positions 0-7 over a boxed row of |PRECEDENCE|D|T|R|0|0| -- same false-positive mechanism as Figure 4, at smaller scale.

math_notes: No mathematical notation (this is a networking protocol specification, not a math document); the bit-position numbering in the diagrams could be mistaken for numeric/math content by an overzealous detector, but it is diagram labeling, not math.

notes_for_implementer: This fixture concentrates THREE separate instances of the exact false-positive-table risk named in the original task brief ('architecture diagrams'), at three different levels of table-likeness: Figure 3 (a loosely box-drawn network diagram), Figure 4 (a highly regular, extremely table-like 32-bit header layout diagram), and the Type-of-Service bit diagram (a smaller version of the same pattern).
